newsitem.title: USA: Marks Bros sees higher Q4 pro forma EPS.
newsitem.headline: Marks Bros sees higher Q4 pro forma EPS.

text.p: Marks Bros Jewelers Inc said Monday it expects pro forms earnings for the fourth quarter ending January 31 of $0.58-$0.60 per share, compared to pro forma earnings of $0.54 a year earlier.
The company also said its same-store sales for the November and December holiday shopping season were flat compared to 1995, while total sales rose 11.2 percent, to $49 million.
Same-store sales were lower than expected, in part because there were five fewer shopping days between Thanksgiving and Christmas in 1996 than in 1995, it said.
Marks Bros also cited "an extremely competitive and promotional environment among jewelry retailers."

"While we are disappointed with our comparable-store sales performance during the holiday, we were able to achieve higher merchandise gross margins above last year's levels while maintaining tight control over our operating expenses," Chairman and Chief Executive Hugh Patinkin said in a statement.

The company's projection of pro forma results reflects its equity offerings and debt recapitalization on May 2 and November 1, 1996. Pro forma results exclude an extraordinary loss on the extinguishment of debt in the fourth quarter, apply a 40 percent tax provision to 1995 pro forma net income from operations, and excludes a one-time income tax benefit in the 1995 fourth quarter.
